chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subbah, who said:
"When a man marries a woman while he is unable to have intercourse with women, he is given a year's respite until he treats himself."
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for a husband who is unable to have intercourse with his wife?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling which establishes a one-year grace period for an impotent husband to seek treatment or recover, balancing the wife's right to annulment (*khiyar al-ayb*) with the possibility of cure. This period allows for medical or natural recovery before the marriage is dissolved, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving the marital bond where feasible. The ruling underscores the legal concept of 'defect' (*ayb*) as a ground for annulment while providing a structured timeline for resolution.
